dimensions.assessment: Applies to Members of Congress, congressional employees, and governmental entities seeking legal process.
dimensions.evidence: a governmental entity may not... seek or obtain a search warrant, grand jury subpoena, court order... that could reasonably be expected to return any covered material

dimensions.assessment: Imposes strict procedural hurdles, special master appointments, and review delays on government investigations involving congressional records.
dimensions.evidence: the governmental entity may not review materials that are reasonably expected to contain covered material until the date that is 30 days after the date notice is made

dimensions.assessment: The source does not provide figures on federal spending or economic impact.
Creates a new chapter in Title 18, United States Code, regulating search warrants and subpoenas concerning legislative branch records.
dimensions.evidence: Title 18, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end of part II the following: 'CHAPTER 239--CONGRESSIONAL RECORDS'

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent restrictions and statutory procedures in federal criminal code.
dimensions.evidence: Notwithstanding any other provision of Federal or State law, a governmental entity may not...

missing_information: Potential costs associated with appointing special masters and delaying investigations.
importance_detail.rationale: Prohibits governmental entities from obtaining certain congressional records through legal process, subject to criminal investigation exceptions, notification rules, and special master reviews.
